newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka announces further cuts in lending rates.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka announces further cuts in lending rates.

text.p: Croatia's leading commercial bank Zagrebacka Banka on Monday announced further cuts in its lending rates as part of a policy to make capital cheaper.
Zagrebacka will cut the rates for its prime clients by two to four percentage points from May 1, board member Davor Holjevac told a news conference.

"This considerable reduction of interest rates does not bring them to the level of those abroad, but...financing risks on the Croatian market are still not the same as comparable risks abroad," the bank said in press release.
In a bid to lower overall credit costs for its clients, it will also scrap a one-off commission on all short-term credits, Holjevac said.
It will charge 14 percent a year on new short-term kuna credits, with the rates 0.50-1 percentage points higher for longer maturities.

The interest on short-term credits in hard currency have been reduced even more and will range between an annual 9.5 and 15 percent. Longer-term currency loans will also be 0.50-1 points more expensive.
The bank, which recently obtained an investment grade rating from IBCA and Moody's, plans to use it to raise funds abroad and funnel them into new lending operations.

But it may give up the idea of issuing Eurobonds and approach the syndicated loan market instead after being offered excellent terms, a bank source told Reuters. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
